Hello world! This is the IAA Hackathon 2026 team's project site, published from
[almac09/iaa-hackathon-2026](https://github.com/almac09/iaa-hackathon-2026) with GitHub Pages.

## What's here

* **[What the data told us](eda.qmd)**: the team's exploratory data analysis, in one place.
* **[Underwriting calculator](underwriting-calculator.qmd)**: price a single policy with the team's Week 2 model and see
  how each rating factor moves the premium. Switch between example policies, or change any factor yourself.
* **[How a GLM works](how-glms-work.qmd)**: a plain-English guide to the kind of model behind the calculator.
* **[Project management](project-management.qmd)**: how we ran the work, with a timeline of every GitHub issue.

## The challenge

Predict the expected 2025 claim cost of each home and motor policy (buildings, contents and motor), with
claims valued at 31 December 2024. Scoring uses Tweedie deviance (D2).

## The model behind the calculator

The calculator uses Gerard's Week 2 model **C0**, exported for an Excel replica in
`workings/contents/replication/export/excel/`:

| Product | Small claims | Large claims |
|---|---|---|
| Home contents | Tweedie GLM | none (no large-claim split) |
| Motor | Tweedie GLM | GLM, scaled to a generalised Pareto mean excess |
| Buildings | XGBoost (not shown) | GLM |

Buildings isn't in the calculator yet because its small-claim model is gradient-boosted trees, not a GLM.

::: {.callout-note}
Every example policy on this site is made up. No competition data is published here.
:::
